issues.description: Method name/signature mismatch for adding a parent: the problem statement and template expect a PersonService.addParent(Person person, Person parent) method, and PersonResource (and tests) invoke addParent, but the solution's PersonService defines a method named registerParent(Person person, Person parent) instead of addParent. This inconsistency between method names will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the correct API to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method names consistent across all artifacts. Rename the solution's registerParent(...) method to addParent(...) (keeping the same parameters and behavior), or alternatively change PersonResource and tests to call registerParent(...) instead. Ensure the template, tests, REST resource, and service all use the same method name and signature (PersonService.addParent(Person, Person)).

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a PersonService method named addParent(Person, Person) (used by PersonResource and described in the requirements), but the solution implementation defines registerParent(Person, Person) instead. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual operation (adding a parent to a person) creates a mapping barrier: students reading the problem and template will look for addParent but find a differently named method in the solution, causing confusion about the intended API and potentially leading to compilation/mapping mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier names so all artifacts use addParent(Person person, Person parent). Specifically, rename registerParent(...) in the solution to addParent(...) (or add an addParent(...) delegating to registerParent) so the method name matches the problem statement, template, and REST resource usage.
